greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who breaks down every wall of enmity, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord, you are our peace and our reconciliation, Lord have mercy.
Christ, you call us to be vigilant and ready for your coming, Christ have mercy.
Lord, you build us into a dwelling place of your Spirit, Lord have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord speaks of peace to his people.
homily:
We often imagine our lives as a house we are building. We lay the floorboards of our plans, we raise the walls of our ambitions, and we carefully curate the rooms where we hope to spend our future. We are so busy with the construction—the logistics of the day, the blueprints of the week ahead—that we sometimes forget that we are not the primary architects. We are the inhabitants, and more importantly, we are the materials being shaped into something much larger than a single, private dwelling. 

In the first reading today, St. Paul speaks to the Ephesians about a radical shift in identity. He tells them that they are 'no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God.' He describes a structure that is being held together, a temple that is growing. Think of that image: a building that is not static, but living. It is a structure that is constantly being added to, constantly being refined, and constantly held together by a single, immovable capstone: Christ Jesus. 

This is the truth of our existence. We are not isolated units, drifting through a cold, empty cosmos. We are part of a grand, divine architecture. Every one of us is a stone in that temple, and every connection we make—every love we share, every memory we hold—is part of the mortar that binds us to one another and to God. When we feel the ache of distance, when we feel that the rooms of our lives are too quiet, we must remember that we are part of a structure that spans the divide between heaven and earth. We are not separated from those who have gone before us; we are simply in different wings of the same house.

Benjamin Vo understood this, perhaps intuitively, in the way he moved through the world. Think of the way he looked at the horizon. He was a boy who loved the sky, who loved the mechanics of flight, who saw the world as a vast, interconnected network. He loved the idea of 'con chim airlines'—not just as a business or a project, but as a way of bridging the distance, of bringing people together, of making the world smaller and more accessible. He was a boy who looked at his own resources—his piggy bank, his time, his attention—and saw them not as things to be hoarded, but as tools to build a bridge to someone else. When he offered everything he had to help his uncle, he wasn't just being generous; he was participating in the very architecture of the Kingdom. He was showing us that our lives are meant to be poured out, to be used, to be part of the ongoing work of love.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has felt like a structural failure. You look at the floor plan of your life, and you see the space where Ben should be, and the absence feels like a collapse. It is a heavy, disorienting experience. But I want to remind you of what Paul tells us: 'In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.' This is not a metaphor. It is a reality. The love you shared with Ben, the joy you found in his curiosity, the way he would giggle when he talked about his planes—that is not gone. It is built into the very foundation of your family. It is a part of the temple that God is raising up. You are not a family that has been broken; you are a family that is being held together by the One who is the capstone. The distance between you and Ben is not a wall; it is a veil. And the Spirit is the one who moves through that veil, keeping you connected, keeping you held, keeping you one.

There is a temptation, when we are grieving, to try to act as our own architects. We try to redesign the past. We try to shore up the walls of our memories, hoping to keep the pain out or to keep the joy in. We worry about whether we did enough, whether we built the foundation strong enough, whether we were observant enough. Let that go. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the ones who provided the love that allowed him to grow into the beautiful, gentle soul he was. You did not miss anything. You are not the ones responsible for the blueprint of his life; that belongs to the Creator. You are responsible only for the love, and you gave that in abundance. You are not being judged by the silence; you are being invited to rest in the structure that God has built around you.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the geometry of this love better than anyone. You know that the bond you share with Ben is not a matter of geography. It is a matter of the heart. When you look at the planes, when you think of the games you coded together, when you feel the quiet of the house, know that you are a vital part of this living temple. You are the one who carries the legacy of his kindness. You are the one who knows what it means to be a brother, to be a friend, to be a witness to the fact that love is the strongest material in the universe. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance, that it is the most durable thing we possess.

Now, look at the Gospel. Jesus tells us to 'gird your loins and light your lamps.' He calls us to be like servants awaiting a master’s return. This sounds like an instruction for a future event, but it is actually a way of living in the present. To 'gird your loins' is to be ready, to be prepared to move, to be unencumbered by the things that weigh us down. To 'light your lamps' is to keep the flame of hope burning, even when the night is long and the master seems to be delayed. Jesus is telling us that the master is coming, and that when he does, he will not just demand our service—he will serve us. 'He will gird himself, have them recline at table, and proceed to wait on them.' 

Think about that. The God of the universe, the Architect of the temple, the One who holds the stars in place—he is the one who waits on us. He is the one who prepares the banquet. He is the one who invites us to sit down and be refreshed. This is the ultimate fulfillment of our hope. All the longing, all the ache, all the 'what ifs' and all the 'whys'—they are all leading to this moment. They are leading to the banquet where the table is set, where the divide is gone, and where we will be reunited with the ones we love in the presence of the One who loves us most. Ben is already at that table. He is already in the place where the light never fades, where the curiosity is satisfied, and where the joy is complete. And he is waiting for you. He is watching over you with that same gentle, radiant smile, and he is part of the cloud of witnesses that is cheering you on as you walk the path toward the same banquet.

We are living in a time that often feels like a construction site—noisy, dusty, and confusing. We see the world changing, we feel the ground shifting, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can build ourselves. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the capstone. He is inviting us to look at the One who holds it all together. He is inviting us to trust that the structure is sound, that the foundation is deep, and that the architect knows exactly what he is doing. You are not a random collection of moments. You are a masterpiece in progress. You are a dwelling place for the Spirit.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your lamp lit. When you feel the weight of the silence, when you feel the ache of the absence, choose to light the lamp of hope. Choose to do one small act of kindness in Ben’s name, just as you have done with the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a sign, a tangible, physical piece of the temple that you are building. It is a sign that the love that was poured into Ben is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of the poor, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope, you are adding a stone to the temple. You are making the structure stronger. You are keeping the light burning.

Do not be afraid of the ache. It is the price of loving well. It is the mark of a heart that is truly alive. And do not be afraid of the silence. It is not a void; it is a space where God is waiting to serve you. If you listen, if you really listen, you will hear the voice of the Father calling you by name, just as he called Benjamin. You will hear the promise that you are a family of four, forever. You will hear the invitation to keep walking, to keep hoping, to keep trusting. The road is long, and it is sometimes steep, but you are not walking it alone. You are being held by the same hands that hold the universe. You are being loved with a love that has no end. And one day, the journey will reach its destination, and you will understand everything. You will see that every step, every tear, every moment of longing was part of the way home. Keep your eyes on the horizon. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may his face shine upon you as you walk in his peace. Go in the strength of his love.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have died, that they may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ.
For all who grieve, especially those who carry a heavy cross, that God may console them with hope and hold them close in his love.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
You were at that time without Christ,
alienated from the community of Israel
and strangers to the covenants of promise,
without hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off
have become near by the Blood of Christ.For he is our peace, he made both one
and broke down the dividing wall of enmity, through his Flesh,
abolishing the law with its commandments and legal claims,
that he might create in himself one new person in place of the two,
thus establishing peace,
and might reconcile both with God,
in one Body, through the cross,
putting that enmity to death by it.
He came and preached peace to you who were far off
and peace to those who were near,
for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners,
but you are fellow citizens with the holy ones
and members of the household of God, 
built upon the foundation of the Apostles and prophets,
with Christ Jesus himself as the capstone.
Through him the whole structure is held together
and grows into a temple sacred in the Lord;
in him you also are being built together
into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (see 9) The Lord speaks of peace to his people.
I will hear what God proclaims;
the LORD–for he proclaims peace.
Near indeed is his salvation to those who fear him,
glory dwelling in our land.
R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people.
Kindness and truth shall meet;
justice and peace shall kiss.
Truth shall spring out of the earth,
and justice shall look down from heaven.
R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people.
The LORD himself will give his benefits;
our land shall yield its increase.
Justice shall walk before him,
and salvation, along the way of his steps.
R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples: 
“Gird your loins and light your lamps
and be like servants who await their master’s return from a wedding,
ready to open immediately when he comes and knocks.
Blessed are those servants
whom the master finds vigilant on his arrival.
Amen, I say to you, he will gird himself,
have them recline at table, and proceed to wait on them.
And should he come in the second or third watch
and find them prepared in this way,
blessed are those servants.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
